idiom_name: CompletableDeferred per request awaited under withTimeout
implementation_notes: Kotlin's coroutines make the reply an awaitable value: the request carries a CompletableDeferred<Reply> (or the caller bridges a callback API with suspendCancellableCoroutine) and awaits it under withTimeout or withTimeoutOrNull, which cancels the wait and propagates through the structured-concurrency scope. The correlation table is replaced by the deferred instance itself, and Channel is the variant for actor-style mailboxes where one consumer answers many requesters; the classic reply-queue structure is only rebuilt when replies arrive on a shared stream with no per-request handle.
pitfalls: withTimeout cancels the awaiting coroutine, not the remote work: the replier needs a deadline in the envelope or a cancellation message, or it keeps processing abandoned requests.
A deferred completed after the timeout is silently ignored, so late replies disappear unless they are logged or dead-lettered.
suspendCancellableCoroutine must be resumed exactly once; a callback that also fires on error paths corrupts the continuation.
